newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Republicans see chance for budget progress.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Republicans see chance for budget progress.

text.p: Senate Republicans said Tuesday Congress and the White House have a good opportunity to move toward a balanced budget next session, but did not expect substantive negotiations until after President Clinton submits his annual budget plan to Congress next year.

Speaking to reporters after a meeting of Republican leaders, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said he thought there was a "very good" opportunity for lawmakers and the White House to make progress on a balanced budget.
Clinton will meet with congressional leaders at the White House later Tuesday.

Republicans said a balanced budget amendment to the U.S. constitution would be a top priority, although they had not yet set a date for a vote. They also reiterated their call for Clinton to take the lead on Medicare reforms.
"The reality is that the election sent a message that people wanted to see a balanced budget," said Florida Republican Sen. Connie Mack.
Oklahoma Republican Sen. Don Nickles said tax relief was still a top item. Both Clinton and Republicans have endorsed middle class tax cuts, though their plans are very different.
